title: Generic Cartier pullback of the translated negative theta divisor
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], $C/k$ a smooth projective connected curve of genus $g\geq1$ [def-sc-curves, def-kun-projective, def-sc-genus], $P\in C(k)$, and $(J,\varphi)$ a Jacobian with its representing isomorphism [def-sc-jacobian]. Write $f_P(Q)=[\mathcal O_C(Q-P)]$. For $0\leq r\leq g$, let $C^{(r)}$ be the scheme of effective degree-$r$ divisors, $f_P^{(r)}(D)=[\mathcal O_C(D-rP)]$ its Abel morphism, and $W_r$ its scheme-theoretic image, as in [lem-sfb-symmetric-abel-image-geometry]. Put $\Theta=W_{g-1}$ and $\Theta^-=[-1]_J^*\Theta$. For $a\in J(k)$ write $t_a(x)=x+a$ and $\Theta^-+a=t_{-a}^*\Theta^-$. There exists a dense open subscheme $U\subseteq J$ such that, for every $a\in U(k)$, exactly one effective divisor $D(a)$ of degree $g$ maps to $a$ under $f_P^{(g)}$, this divisor is a sum of $g$ distinct points, and
$$f_P^*(\Theta^-+a)=D(a)$$
as effective Cartier divisors on $C$ (closed subschemes locally cut out by a non-zero-divisor) [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle], where $\Theta^-+a$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $J$ and the left side is its scheme-theoretic inverse image under $f_P$. In particular,
$$f_P^*\mathcal O_J(\Theta^-+a)\cong\mathcal O_C(D(a)).$$
Divisors on $C$ are as in [def-sc-divisor], the invertible module $\mathcal O_J(\Theta^-+a)$ associated with an effective Cartier divisor is that of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle], invertible sheaves are as in [def-sc-invertible-module], and sheaf pullback is [def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Chapter III Lemma 6.7, printed pp.105–106, including density of U and equality as Cartier divisors; notation for the translated inversion image of Theta immediately before Theorem 6.6.

proof.text: Write $H_r=C^{(r)}$ and $a_r=f_P^{(r)}$. The curve $C$ is integral with discrete valuation local rings by [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings], proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper], and geometrically integral by [prop-pc-xk-integral]. The Hilbert schemes $H_r$ are smooth proper varieties by [thm-pc-hilb-curves] and geometrically integral by [lem-sc-hilb-geometrically-integral]; they are locally Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. The fixed Jacobian is an abelian variety [def-sc-jacobian, def-sc-abelian-variety]; [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization] makes $J$ integral, and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] makes it locally Noetherian. It is quasi-compact since it is proper. By [lem-sfb-symmetric-abel-image-geometry], $\Theta=W_{g-1}$ is integral and an effective Cartier divisor, and $a_g:H_g\to J$ and $a_{g-1}:H_{g-1}\to\Theta$ are birational. The closed subscheme $\Theta$ is locally Noetherian: on an affine open of $J$ its ring is a quotient of a Noetherian ring. It is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper].

source.place: III 6.7, first paragraph, using III 5.1(a); Stacks 0B9I (pic-proposition-hilb-d).

proof.text: The map $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field], locally of finite presentation by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and universally open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. Apply [lem-sfb-integral-pullback-geometric-flat-open] with second factor $H_{g-1}$ and then $\Theta$: both $X=C\times H_{g-1}$ and $Y=C\times\Theta$ are integral. They are proper over $k$: use [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] for one projection and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] for the structure map. Define $h=1_C\times a_{g-1}:X\to Y$ and $\psi:Y\to J$ by $\psi(Q,b)=f_P(Q)+b$. The three maps $a_g,a_{g-1},\psi$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated], since their sources are proper over $k$ and their targets are separated (for $\Theta$, this follows already from its properness). In particular the Abel maps have closed image [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image]. Their birationality makes their images dense, so they are surjective. By [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], $h$ and every base change of $h$ are surjective.

source.place: III 6.7, degree-comparison map C times Theta to J; Stacks 01S1 (morphisms-lemma-base-change-surjective).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-birational-generic-isomorphism-open] to the proper birational Abel maps. Their targets are Noetherian: $J$ is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian, and $\Theta$ is closed in $J$. Obtain dense opens $V_g\subset J$ and $V_{g-1}\subset\Theta$ over whose full inverse images the respective maps are isomorphisms. In particular each $a\in V_g(k)$ has a unique effective degree-$g$ divisor $D(a)$. Moreover $h$ is an isomorphism over $C\times V_{g-1}$, a nonempty open in the integral scheme $Y$. Its inverse image is nonempty open in the integral scheme $X$, so $h$ identifies their generic points and function fields.

source.place: III 6.7, zero-dimensional Abel-fibre open; III 5.1(a); Stacks 0BAJ (morphisms-lemma-birational-isomorphism-over-dense-open).

proof.text: We also need a nonempty open $R_g\subset H_g$ of reduced divisors. If $g=1$, take $R_1=H_1=C$. If $g\geq2$, let $\beta:C\times H_{g-2}\to H_g$, $(Q,E)\mapsto2Q+E$, be the composite of $(Q,E)\mapsto(Q,Q+E)$ with $(Q,F)\mapsto Q+F$, both given by the addition morphisms of [lem-pc-hilb-addition] (applied to the separated smooth morphism $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ of relative dimension $1$, all of whose Hilbert functors are representable by [thm-pc-hilb-curves]); on rational points they add the divisor of a rational point, so $\beta(Q,E)=2Q+E$ for rational $Q,E$. Its source is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]; hence $\beta$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] and has closed image by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image]. Put $R_g=H_g\setminus\beta(C\times H_{g-2})$. It is nonempty: [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] and the integral dimension-one curve imply that, after deleting any finite set of closed points, a rational point remains. Inductively choose $g$ distinct points. Their sum cannot equal $2Q+E$, by the nonnegative coefficients of effective divisors [def-sc-divisor]. Over algebraically closed $k$, every closed point of any fibre of $\beta$ is rational, by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space, lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. Consequently a degree-$g$ divisor lies in this image precisely when it has a repeated point; thus $R_g(k)$ consists exactly of sums of $g$ distinct points. Since $H_g$ is integral, $R_g$ is dense.

source.place: III 6.7, removal of the images of repeated-point diagonals; Stacks 0B9I (pic-proposition-hilb-d), addition morphisms.

proof.text: Let $\alpha:X=C\times H_{g-1}\to H_g$ be the addition morphism of [lem-pc-hilb-addition] (with $d=g-1$, the factors swapped), sending a $T$-point $(Q,E)$ to the scheme-theoretic sum $Q+E$, whose ideal is the product of the ideals of $E$ and of the graph of $Q$. It is finite locally free of rank $g$ by [lem-pc-hilb-addition], the case $(1,g-1)$ of the rank $\binom g1$ of [thm-pc-hilb-curves]. The Abel formulas give the equality of morphisms $\psi h=a_g\alpha$: tensoring $\mathcal O_C(Q-P)$ and $\mathcal O_C(E-(g-1)P)$ gives $\mathcal O_C(Q+E-gP)$. This is an identity of families, hence of morphisms by the representing isomorphism [def-sc-jacobian], not just an identity on rational points. Above $V_g$, $a_g$ is an isomorphism, so $(\psi h)^{-1}(V_g)\to V_g$ is finite locally free of rank $g$. Over the generic point $\eta$ of $J$, $h_\eta$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Its source is finite over $k(\eta)$, so the underlying generic fibre of $\psi$ is finite as well.

source.place: III 6.7, degree calculation; Stacks 0B9I, addition H_1 times H_(g-1) to H_g, replaces the equivalent factorial degree calculation.

proof.text: The proper map $\psi$ is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and of finite type. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-generic-finite-morphism-open-neighborhood] using its finite generic fibre, then [lem-sbc-generic-flatness] on the resulting integral base open. Shrink further to an affine neighbourhood $F$ of $\eta$ with a finite free basis of rank $n$ supplied by [lem-sbc-finite-flat-affine-basis]. In fact $n=g$. To check this without a fibre-rank inequality, use [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] to identify the function field of either integral source with the fraction field of any nonempty affine open. For a finite dominant map of integral affine schemes, tensoring the finite domain algebra with the base fraction field is a finite-dimensional domain, hence a field (multiplication by each nonzero element is injective and therefore surjective); it is thus the source fraction field. Consequently $n=[k(Y):k(J)]$. Similarly the rank-$g$ composite over $V_g$ gives $g=[k(X):k(J)]$. The birational map $h$ identified these fields over $k(J)$ in Step 3, so $n=g$. Thus $\psi^{-1}(F)\to F$ is finite locally free of rank $g$.

source.place: III 6.7, final paragraph: replace the unproved normal-base fibre-rank bound by shrinking to a finite flat open. Stacks 02NW (morphisms-lemma-generically-finite), 052A (morphisms-proposition-generic-flatness), 02KB (morphisms-lemma-finite-flat).

proof.text: The isomorphism $a_g^{-1}(V_g)\simeq V_g$ carries $R_g\cap a_g^{-1}(V_g)$ to a nonempty open $V_g^{\mathrm{red}}\subset J$: the intersection is nonempty since $H_g$ is integral and both opens are nonempty. Put $U=F\cap V_g^{\mathrm{red}}$. This is nonempty, open and dense since $J$ is integral. Every $a\in U(k)$ has its unique divisor $D(a)=P_1+\cdots+P_g$ with all $P_i$ distinct, and the fibre $E_a=Y\times_J\{a\}$ of $\psi$ is finite of $k$-vector-space rank $g$.

source.place: III 6.7, intersect the degree-comparison open with the unique reduced-divisor open.

proof.text: The first projection identifies $E_a$ with the closed subscheme $f_P^{-1}(\Theta^-+a)$ of $C$. Indeed for every test scheme $T$, its pairs $(Q,b)$ satisfy $b\in\Theta(T)$ and $f_P(Q)+b=a_T$; eliminating $b$ gives $a_T-f_P(Q)\in\Theta(T)$, equivalently $f_P(Q)\in\Theta^-+a$. These constructions are inverse and functorial, so the identification is scheme-theoretic [def-pc-fibre-product]. The base change of $h$ onto $E_a$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Its source is $\alpha^{-1}(D(a))$, since $a_g$ is an isomorphism above $a$. By the effective-divisor description of rational points in [thm-pc-hilb-curves] and the formula $\alpha(Q,E)=Q+E$ on rational points of [lem-pc-hilb-addition], its rational points are exactly $(P_i,D(a)-P_i)$, $1\leq i\leq g$. All its points are closed and rational, since it is finite over algebraically closed $k$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. Their images in $E_a\subset C$ are the distinct $P_i$. Surjectivity therefore shows that the support of $E_a$ is exactly $\{P_1,\ldots,P_g\}$.

source.place: III 6.7, support calculation and identification of the incidence fibre with the inverse-image subscheme; Stacks 01S1.

proof.text: Write $E_a=\operatorname{Spec}B$. This is a finite $k$-algebra of dimension $g$ with $g$ distinct rational points. Evaluation $B\to k^g$ is surjective: for each $i\ne j$, choose $c_{ij}$ in the maximal ideal of $P_j$ but not that of $P_i$, and divide by its nonzero value at $P_i$; the product over $j\ne i$ has evaluation the $i$th standard basis vector. Equal dimensions now make evaluation an isomorphism. Thus $E_a$ is the reduced closed subscheme on these points. By [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings], at $P_i$ its ideal is the maximal ideal of a discrete valuation ring, generated by a uniformizer, and elsewhere it is the unit ideal. This proves that $E_a$ is the effective Cartier divisor $\sum_i[P_i]=D(a)$, including each multiplicity. Inversion and translation are scheme isomorphisms, so their pullbacks of the local non-zero-divisor equations of $\Theta$ are again such equations; hence $\Theta^-+a$ is effective Cartier too [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle].

source.place: III 6.7, equality as Cartier divisors: rank g and g distinct support points force all multiplicities to be one.

proof.text: Finally, on an open of $J$ with Cartier equation $s$ for $\Theta^-+a$, the ideal has basis $s$ and its dual has basis $s^\vee$. Its pullback has the corresponding basis, and the ideal of $E_a$ has basis $f_P^\#s$, a non-zero-divisor by Step 9. Send the pulled-back dual basis to $(f_P^\#s)^\vee$. If an equation changes to $us$ for a unit $u$, both dual bases change by $(f_P^\#u)^{-1}$, so these isomorphisms glue. By [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle, def-pc-module-pullback] this gives $f_P^*\mathcal O_J(\Theta^-+a)\simeq\mathcal O_C(E_a)$. Substitute $E_a=D(a)$ and use [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-agrees-sc] for the curve divisor convention. No flatness of the Abel embedding is asserted or needed.

source.place: III 6.7, associated invertible sheaves, by the local Cartier-ideal definition (Stacks 0C4U).
